subject: Prism AI - Dedicated GPU sizing + SLO fit for Pilot
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@prismai.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated sizing ask — expected TPS & headroom for 6-week pilot

Hi Irene / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We want to scope the dedicated pool for the 6-week pilot: target 99th pct gen latency <= 350ms for single-turn completions, with an expected steady-state of ~200 concurrent users and occasional bursts up to 800 concurrent. Average prompt length will be ~120 tokens; responses ~240 tokens.

Can you share a sizing sketch (tokens/sec per GPU, recommended cluster size, and a recommended headroom policy) that maps to those SLOs? We need this for our procurement and to justify reserved capacity.

Also attaching a quick traffic sketch.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Lin
Head of Cloud Ops, Prism AI
Attachment: prism_traffic_sketch.pdf (pdf)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@prismai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing ask — expected TPS & headroom for 6-week pilot

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear constraints. Attached is a short working calc and a couple of options (conservative vs. aggressive) for the pilot. High-level summary below; full calculations are in prism_poc_capacity_calc.xlsx.

Summary (assumptions)
- Model: open-llm-70b-2q (quantized) — measured median tokens/sec per A100-80GB equivalent ~17k for generation at 1k prompt+response sequence length; for your average sequence (~360 tokens total) we observed ~38k tokens/sec per GPU under continuous batching.
- SLO target: 99th latency <= 350ms — map to target tokens-per-second that preserves per-request latency budget when burst preemption is considered.

Sizing options (steady-state 200 concurrent users -> ~200 rps at peak user activity):
1) Conservative (recommended for initial pilot)
- Effective TPS needed (accounting for tails & small-batch penalty): 200 concurrent * (360 tokens / avg_response_time) approximated => we instead compute token demand from requests: assume 0.6 reqs/sec per concurrent user during peak => 120 rps * 360 tokens = 43,200 tokens/sec.
- Per-GPU effective sustained TPS (with batching + caching): 28,000 tokens/sec (safe operating point).
- GPUs required: ceil(43,200 / 28,000) = 2 GPUs -> but add headroom & HA => recommend 4 GPUs (2 active + 2 spare/burst).
- Notes: This keeps 99th latency headroom for single-turn completion under 350ms in our test harness.

2) Aggressive (cost-optimized)
- Assume better batching and prefetched KV-cache: effective TPS per GPU = 38,000 tokens/sec.
- GPUs required: ceil(43,200 / 38,000) = 2 -> recommend 3 GPUs (reduce spare to 1).

Burst handling
- For short bursts up to 800 concurrent, autoscaling/burst capacity model: request temporary burst pool of +4 GPUs (cold-start < 1 min expected for new instances); use token-bucket throttling policy at 95th pct to protect latency.

Operational recommendations
- Canary rollout: pin model variant and enable automatic fallback to a smaller model for non-critical paths.
- Start with conservative config (4 GPUs) and observe 7-day traffic, then reduce if measured effective TPS per GPU > 32k.
- Instrumentation: per-route token counters, p99 latency tracing, and the sample prompt set for regression detection (we can onboard your sample prompts into Redwood Eval).

I attached the workbook with line-by-line math and an SLA-fit visualization. Quick Qs: what cold-start tolerance can you accept for burst scale? Also confirm whether you prefer reserved-only or reserved + burst billing.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: prism_poc_capacity_calc.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@prismai.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-19T10:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing ask — recommended contract framing

Adding a quick note on procurement framing and deal economics.

- For a 6-week pilot we typically recommend a short-term Dedicated reservation (monthly pro-rated) for 4 GPUs to avoid frequent scale churn — this also gives Prism visibility on committed throughput for the pilot.
- Pricing guidance: pilot rate = ~0.65x of full committed monthly rate for a short-term reservation; if Prism converts to a 12-month commitment we can reprice to reflect committed capacity discounts.
- Deal mechanics: include a documented burst allowance (on-demand GPUs up to +4) with a defined cold-start SLA and a billing uplift for burst minutes.

I'll prepare a one-page mutual action plan and a draft reservation term sheet that matches the 4-GPU conservative recommendation unless we see telemetry that supports the aggressive option.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: prism_pilot_term_sheet_draft.docx (docx)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@prismai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-21T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing ask — follow-up & next steps

Thanks all — Sarah, quick clarifications before I send the MAP and term sheet:
1) Can you confirm average requests per user per minute during peak? Irene used 0.6 reqs/sec per active user in the calc; if you expect lower (0.2-0.4) that materially shrinks token demand.
2) Do you want us to include an explicit SLA for cold-start (<60s for scaling up) in the pilot term sheet? That has operational tradeoffs.

Proposed next steps:
- Sarah confirms the user behavior numbers (1) and burst tolerance (2) by Thu 6/24.
- We deliver MAP + pilot reservation quote by Fri 6/25.
- Kickoff for provisioning planned Mon 6/28 pending signed pilot SOW.

Also marking action items: 
- Irene: finalize workbook lines for the 4-GPU conservative config and add a sensitivity column for request rate variance.
- Marissa: draft MAP + term sheet (pilot).

Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
